clue.text: Went on a bicycle, say, one's to get off in a state

indicators.note: say tells us to go by how the phrase sounds when spoken, not by its spelling

parts.note: to go on a bicycle is to ride it, so went on one is rode
one is I, so one's (one is) gives I and S
to land is to get off a vehicle or come down from the air

explanation.surface: A cyclist is told that someone has to dismount somewhere within a certain state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks a sound-alike: RODE, spoken, is the RHODE of the state's name. 'One's' is read as 'one is', I + S.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhode Island is the smallest of the fifty American states, in New England.

clue.text: The man married and was given the chop

parts.note: a man is referred to as he
to wed is to marry, so married is wed

explanation.surface: A man got married and was promptly sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: Hewing is cutting with an axe, so something hewed has been chopped.

clue.text: She distressed Samson!

parts.note: distressed is read as de-tressed: the biblical woman who had the strongman's hair cut off, taking away his tresses and his strength

explanation.surface: A woman upset the biblical strongman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distressed' looks like 'upset', but the clue means de-tressed: she had his locks shorn in the Book of Judges.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible the Philistine woman betrayed Samson by having his seven locks of hair shaved off.

clue.text: Annie's removed crackers

indicators.note: removed suggests the letters are moved about, so the name and its possessive ending are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone named Annie has taken away the Christmas crackers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' is the anagram signal: re-moved, its letters moved again. The S of the possessive counts here.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackers is British slang for mad, the same sense as out of one's mind.

clue.text: Bert, toil over the words of the opera

indicators.note: over, in the sense of turned over, tells us to rearrange the letters of the two words before it

explanation.surface: Bert is told to labour away at writing the text for an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' looks like 'labour over', but it is the anagram signal on BERT and TOIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A libretto is the text of an opera, the lines that are sung and spoken.

clue.text: Lily or Leonard went up to the boss

indicators.note: in a down clue, went up means the word is read from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: Len is a short form of the name Leonard
an umbo is the boss, the raised centre, of a shield

explanation.surface: Either Lily or Leonard climbed the stairs to see their employer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the boss' suggests an employer, but it is the knob on a shield, UMBO. 'went up' turns LEN to NEL in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelumbo is the botanical genus of the lotus, a water plant commonly called a lily.

clue.text: How one may feel among heavenly apparitions?

definitions.text: How one may feel among heavenly apparitions?

parts.words: How one may feel among heavenly apparitions?
parts.note: a cheerful mood is described literally as being placed amid lofty ghosts, heavenly apparitions being spirits up on high

explanation.surface: Someone wonders how it feels to be surrounded by angels.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for very cheerful, while literally it puts someone among elevated ghosts.

clue.text: Its value may go up as it is passed down

definitions.text: Its value may go up as it is passed down

parts.words: Its value may go up as it is passed down
parts.note: handed down the generations while its worth rises, the up and down set against each other

explanation.surface: Something gains worth while being lowered.
explanation.definitionFit: An heirloom is a family treasure inherited by each generation, often appreciating as an antique.

clue.text: Fair exchange in sight?

parts.note: a fair exchange is equal retaliation, and in sight hints that the organ of vision is what is swapped

explanation.surface: Someone sees a fair trade coming up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in sight' seems to mean 'coming soon', but it points to the eye, the thing exchanged in the old law of retaliation.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical law of retaliation demands equal punishment, so the injury done is returned in kind.

clue.text: Post offering support ton the way up perhaps

definitions.text: Post offering support ton the way up perhaps

parts.words: Post offering support ton the way up perhaps
parts.note: a post that supports a stair handrail at the bottom or top of a flight, the way up being the staircase

explanation.surface: Something gives backing to a person climbing the career ladder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way up' suggests a rising career, but it is a staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: A newel is the upright pillar at the foot or head of a staircase holding the banister.

clue.text: Second lieutenant of inferior rank

definitions.meaning: a junior army officer below captain

explanation.surface: A junior officer is described as lowly.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the army term for a junior officer, and as an adjective it means subordinate.

clue.text: None idle? Could be about 100 suffering from idleness

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the next piece
could be says the letters of the two words before it might form something else when rearranged

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: Asking whether nobody is lazy, it reckons about a hundred are afflicted by sloth.
explanation.walkthrough: The question 'None idle?' reads as surface chatter but is the fodder; 'suffering from' is a link joining wordplay to the definition, leaving INDOLEN + E around C.
explanation.definitionFit: Indolence is laziness, an avoidance of activity or effort.

clue.text: Cheerful when slightly drunk

definitions.meaning: tipsy, a little the worse for drink

explanation.surface: Someone is cheery when a little tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means jolly, and in British use also tipsy after a few drinks.

clue.text: Full extent of a rise

definitions.meaning: the peak or utmost degree, as in the top of fashion

explanation.surface: Someone measures the full scale of an increase.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means the utmost point of something, and also an elevated place or hill.

clue.text: How one might get a bright idea?

definitions.text: How one might get a bright idea?

parts.words: How one might get a bright idea?
parts.note: an idea arriving instantly is pictured literally as coming in a burst of bright light

explanation.surface: Someone wonders how inspiration strikes.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for instantly, and a flash is a burst of bright light.

clue.text: Kept at a distance when suspended temporarily from one's job

explanation.surface: Someone stayed aloof after being temporarily laid off.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means held at bay, and also laid off temporarily from work.

clue.text: To some place new, Ray and he resort

indicators.note: resort, read as re-sort, says the letters of the words before it are sorted again into a new order

explanation.surface: A man called Ray and a companion head off to a fresh holiday destination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday spot, but it is the anagram signal on NEW RAY HE.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means to any place whatever, wherever one likes.

clue.text: Commending fruit that has been dried in Portugal

annotationWithheld.why: Commending fruit that has been dried in Portugal: RAISIN inside P (Portugal) gives PRAISIN; nothing in the clue as held supplies the final G
annotationWithheld.clue: Commending fruit that has been dried in Portugal

clue.text: Score four less

parts.note: a score is twenty, and taking four from it is the arithmetic the clue asks for

explanation.surface: A match result is reduced by four.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is twenty, and twenty minus four is the number one more than fifteen.

clue.text: Counterfeit coin must be replaced, about to be returned

indicators.note: be replaced says the letters of the word before it are put back in another order
to be returned means the next piece is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: re is Latin for about, concerning, as in business letters

explanation.surface: A fake coin has to be swapped and sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be replaced' shuffles MUST into STUM; 'to be returned' reverses RE to ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Stumer is old British slang for a dud cheque or a forged coin.

clue.text: Esther, a remarkable lady

indicators.note: remarkable, read as re-markable, suggests the letters of the name and the article can be marked out afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: The biblical queen is praised as an outstanding woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remarkable' seems to praise Esther, but it is the anagram signal on ESTHER A.
explanation.definitionFit: Theresa is a woman's first name, so it names a particular lady.

clue.text: Confusion when hash is finished

parts.note: to make a hash of something is to make a mess of it
up means over or finished, as in time is up

explanation.surface: The dish of hash is all gone, leaving everyone bewildered.
explanation.definitionFit: A mess-up is a muddle or blunder, a state of disorder.

clue.text: Take it easy, have some more laxatives!

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone advises calm and another dose of laxatives.
explanation.definitionFit: To relax is to rest and unwind, letting go of tension.

clue.text: Immediately after which when rope snagged trapping you, it was said

indicators.note: trapping means the jumbled letters close around the next piece
snagged suggests a tangle, so the letters of the two words before it are jumbled
it was said tells us to take the word by its sound, so the pronoun becomes a single letter

parts.note: the pronoun spoken aloud is the letter U

explanation.surface: A rope snags and catches someone, and that is what was reported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snagged' looks like the rope catching, but it jumbles the two words before it into WHENROPE letters; 'it was said' gives U, the letter that sounds like the pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means directly following which, used to link one event to the next.

clue.text: Not quite through, it's almost out of date

indicators.note: not quite means the word is cut short, its final letter dropped

parts.note: passed means got through, as in an exam or a round

explanation.surface: Something nearly finished is almost past its sell-by date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' drops the last letter of PASSED. 'it's almost' leans on the definition, the word being one letter short of passed.
explanation.definitionFit: The French loanword means old-fashioned, no longer in style.

clue.text: Sense a smaller number do not have a flavour

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for an adjective: things that do not have a flavour are flavourless

parts.note: taste is one of the five senses
less means a smaller amount or number

explanation.surface: Someone senses that fewer dishes lack any flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is insipid has no savour at all.

clue.text: Literary effort?

parts.note: an effort is an attempt, and a literary one is a short written composition

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a piece of writing counts as a real attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a short prose composition and also, in older use, an attempt or trial.

clue.text: Up to your neck in it?

definitions.text: Up to your neck in it?

parts.words: Up to your neck in it?
parts.note: being in serious trouble is pictured literally as standing in water up to the chin

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether you are submerged to the chin.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in serious trouble, pictured as water too high to stand in safely.
